model.description: Model name the agent requests. A name no adapter supplies exercises the eager side of the stream boundary.

expect_causes.description: Per completed turn, the origins of the inputs that caused it. Under claim-all one turn carries several, which a singular turn origin could not express.

expect_assistant_stop_reasons.description: Stop reason of each assistant message reaching model history, in order.

expect_assistant_details.description: The full public AssistantMessage shape (design spec section 4) for each assistant message reaching model history, in order -- parallel to expect_assistant_stop_reasons but exhaustive rather than stop-reason-only. Every field the real object carries must be given exactly; optional fields absent from the real message are asserted as null, not omitted, so a scenario cannot silently skip checking one.

listeners.description: Declarative listeners on the tools pipeline. Block and result transformation are listener behaviors; without this a scenario cannot express them.

expect_tool_completion_order.description: Tool call ids in the order their tools finished. Distinct from message order by design (design spec section 6).

expect_request_tools.description: Tool names offered to the model, per request in order. Pins what registration and withdrawal actually change.

expect_updates.description: Live tool_execution_update observations, in emission order (TOOL-017, IR-L06-005) -- a late update (after the tool settles) must never appear here. `arguments` is the ORIGINAL tool-call arguments (before prepare_arguments/validation), matching pinned Pi's own tool_execution_update payload exactly.

expect_tool_trace.description: Language-neutral execution-order evidence (IR-L06-001): each entry names a stage (`start`/`before`/`execute`/`end`) and the tool_call_id it belongs to, in the exact order production actually emitted them. `start`/`end` correspond to tool_execution_start/tool_execution_end; `before` marks the moment a call's before-hook waterfall has fully settled (Proceed or Block), regardless of registered listeners; `execute` marks the moment a prepared call's execute() body begins running. Proves the sequential-preflight-then-concurrent-execute barrier directly against the real production executor -- the runner does not construct this ordering, only observes it.

expect_error.description: The scenario is expected to raise. Only the eager side of the stream boundary does: once a stream is returned, nothing escapes iteration.

arguments.description: The original tool-call arguments -- before prepare_arguments/validation -- matching pinned Pi's own PreparedToolCall.toolCall.arguments, not the value execute() actually runs with.

only_tool.description: Apply to calls naming this tool only. Without it a policy listener would have to be written per scenario.

truncated.description: End the raw provider stream without a terminal chunk. The service must settle it as an error rather than raising.

chunks_after_terminal.description: Extra chunks a misbehaving provider emits after its terminal. The public stream must fuse and deliver none of them.

response_model.description: Concrete model when different from the requested model (design spec section 4).

response_id.description: Provider-specific response/message identifier, when the upstream API exposes one.

raw_stop_reason.description: The provider's own stop-reason string, preserved alongside the normalized stop_reason.

text_signature.description: Opaque provider replay metadata preserving Responses-family message item identity/phase (design spec section 4).

thinking_signature.description: Opaque provider replay metadata: the complete provider reasoning item needed for Responses-family replay.

redacted.description: Whether the provider redacted this thinking block's visible text.

thought_signature.description: Opaque provider-specific replay metadata used by APIs that need it; cross-model transformation strips it.

namespace.description: The tool namespace this call belongs to, when a provider distinguishes tools by more than name alone.

cost.description: Monetary cost matching Usage's token breakdown (design spec section 4).

diagnostic.description: AssistantMessageDiagnostic: redacted provider/runtime diagnostics for failures and recoveries (design spec section 4).

deferredHandle.description: A pending async/deferred provider response, polled or resumed later (design spec section 4).

assistantMessageDetail.description: The exhaustive public AssistantMessage shape (design spec section 4), normalized from a real object the implementation produced -- every field required so a scenario cannot silently omit one it should be checking. Optional Pi fields absent from the real message are represented as null, not omitted. `role` is intentionally omitted: this definition only ever normalizes AssistantMessage instances, so role is always the constant "assistant" and carries no information -- the definition's own name encodes it instead.

parameters.$comment: The actual Layer-05 shared ToolDefinition.parameters representation -- a plain, object-valued JSON Schema mapping -- passed straight through to the production validator, never a Python-specific shorthand (L06-R001). Omitted defaults to the explicit empty-object schema.

raises.description: prepare_arguments throws this message instead of running (TOOL-017).

set.description: Keys to overwrite/add on the arguments before validation.

emits_updates.description: Partial-output values the tool reports, in order, before returning (TOOL-017).

late_update.description: A partial-output value the tool reports one cooperative scheduler tick AFTER it has already returned -- must be silently ignored (TOOL-017).
